record_type_quote: The claim selected for replication from Srinivasan and Carey (2010) was the Experiment 3 claim that participants who were familiarised with congruent pairings of line lengths and tone duration (e.g., long line, long tone) spontaneously accessed the structural similarity between representations, allowing for precise encoding of these pairings, supporting more accurate detection of novel vs. familiar items, compared with participants familiarised with incongruent pairings (e.g., long line, short tone).

targets.title: The long and the short of it: On the nature and origin of functional overlap between representations of space and time.
targets.evidence_quote: The claim selected for replication from Srinivasan and Carey (2010) was the Experiment 3 claim that participants who were familiarised with congruent pairings of line lengths and tone duration (e.g., long line, long tone) spontaneously accessed the structural similarity between representations, allowing for precise encoding of these pairings, supporting more accurate detection of novel vs. familiar items, compared with participants familiarised with incongruent pairings (e.g., long line, short tone).
targets.outcome_quote: In the results quoted above, Srinivasan and Carey (2010) reported p-values for 11 effects. We replicated all seven that were p < .05. We observed p < .05 for the four effects that Srinivasan and Carey (2010) reported as non-significant. However the size and direction of our effects were consistent with the trends reported in the original paper.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The SCORE H* group-by-novelty claim is explicitly replicated, but this is one effect rather than an overall verdict. Preregistered additional analyses deliberately retest the first two paragraphs of original section 4.2; the side-by-side comparisons explicitly show incongruent participants detecting novelty where the original reported they did not, and the final paragraph identifies four original null findings becoming significant. Authors note consistent direction/trends and power as an explanation, yet explicitly identify these differences. This is not mixed merely because the main effect is smaller or because a measure count differs.

reasoning: Entire five-page completed report retests Experiment 3 in a new Bristol sample online. GUID file title, PDF header, OSF node title, and contributors verify assigned identity. Main SCORE claim succeeded; additional explicitly contrasted findings differ, yielding mixed at original-paper level.
